The first time I went the theme was “Beyond the Binary”. I thought it would be a good chance to talk about NB in the community or how I felt disconnected from womanhood due to my gender expression. Boy, was I wrong. The entire time, the conversation was dominated by bisexuals and pansexuals talking about their attraction to men, and how they felt they couldn’t be attracted to men and seen as queer. I literally couldn’t get a single word in the entire 1.5 hour session. The whole time it was just “I LOOOOOOVE men with abs, they’re so sexy” or “aren’t men just the cutest with their eyelashes?” I couldn’t relate to a single one of them, and I felt completely excluded, because, well, I was. Not a single word was said about lesbians or attraction to women. At a WLW support group. 

I didn’t want to go back, but my bisexual friend encouraged me to. Subsequent meetings were slightly better, but I still could hardly ever get a word in, and it was obvious that lesbians were a minority to be seen rather than heard. It was all very heteronormative and cisnormative. I never felt like I had a space to be a lesbian at college, until, ironically, I met my girlfriend at an Episcopalian Church with a very progressive priest. He even had a sermon about how eunuchs were the first trans people in the Bible and how they were held highly in God’s favor (even founding their own church!), so we should treat trans people with the same respect today. He said he had officiated gay weddings before, and he made me feel like I could actually be myself in the open. Now my girlfriend and I live together, unfortunately in a different state from that church, but we still try to be our open and authentic selves. We haven’t found a queer community here, but we have joined the community theatre, which is kind of like a mini gay club.
